elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no affiliate carve-out; the only no-consent exception is "either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets." Assignment to a Customer affiliate remains subject to Vendor's "express, prior written consent." To meet preferred, add an express Customer right to assign to an affiliate without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other party." "Either party" includes Customer (Company), and the permission overrides the preceding consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual carve-out now lets Contractor (Vendor) assign to its own successor in a merger, acquisition, or asset sale on mere written notice, without Customer consent. Under the preferred position Vendor assignment must remain consent-gated; the carve-out would need to be one-way in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard applies to consent for Vendor assignments outside the successor carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears anywhere in the rendered clause; the successor carve-out in fact permits an unconsented Vendor transfer to an acquirer that could be a Customer competitor. An express "and never to a competitor of Company" bar is required.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply on these facts: the document contains no change-of-control provision and Section 6 provides only mutual convenience and breach terminations, so no Vendor termination right is triggered by Customer's change of control and nothing needed deleting.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "[E]ither party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets" — expressly mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The same sentence conditions the successor assignment "upon written notice to the other party."

Retained first sentence: "Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent." The only no-consent exception added is the successor carve-out itself; no affiliate or other non-successor exception was introduced, so the consent gate survives for all other assignments.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained qualifier "which will not be unreasonably withheld" attaches to the consent requirement governing all non-successor assignments.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (mutual successor right, written notice, retained consent gate, retained reasonableness standard). The deviation call is correct because the unamended clause subjected successor assignments to the counterparty's consent, failing the fallback's mutual successor right.

Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Customer, no bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor, and the mutual successor carve-out now allows Vendor to assign to its own successor without Customer consent. If the preferred position is later pursued, make the carve-out one-way (Company only), add "or to an affiliate", and add "and in no event to a competitor of Company".

Walk-away is not engaged: there is no change-of-control provision and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control, so the sixth preferred element is satisfied by absence and required no edit.

Minimal: a single appended sentence, nothing deleted, no survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure. The "Notwithstanding the foregoing" opener is scoped to the immediately preceding sentence rather than functioning as a broad agreement-wide override, so it does not trip the non-minimal override boundary, though a direct "without the other party's consent" formulation would be equally tight.

Preserves intent: the retained consent standard, the subcontracting restriction, and Section 6's termination mechanics all survive without contradiction; the new sentence leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.
